name: Synaptic Overload Gauntlet SOG-3 'Seizure'
description:
The SOG-3 is a full-hand combat gauntlet housing a dense array of transcranial magnetic stimulation coils embedded in the palm and finger assemblies. On contact with a target's skull or upper cervical spine, the gauntlet delivers a precisely timed sequence of high-intensity magnetic pulses that induce involuntary neural firing across multiple cortical regions simultaneously. The result is immediate and total motor control disruption — a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that renders the target non-functional for twelve to forty seconds, followed by a period of profound disorientation lasting several minutes.

The SOG-3's engineering challenge was achieving sufficient field strength for reliable neural induction while maintaining a chassis light enough for combat use. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's solution was a laminated coil architecture using superconductive filament wound at near-molecular density, powered by a forearm-mounted burst capacitor that delivers the full charge in a 0.08-second pulse. The gauntlet requires skin or thin-material contact to function reliably — heavy helmets and full cranial shielding significantly reduce effectiveness, though even partial contact with an unshielded neck produces measurable impairment.

A secondary effect, noted in field reports but absent from official documentation, is the gauntlet's interaction with neural implants. Targets with cognitive augmentations — memory chips, neural co-processors, reflex accelerators — frequently experience device corruption or complete burnout alongside the induced seizure. This has made the SOG-3 particularly feared in circles where neural augmentation is common, as the loss of a high-grade cognitive implant can be professionally and financially devastating beyond the immediate physical harm.
specifications:
effective contact area: Palm and proximal finger pads, 180cm²
pulse duration: 0.08 seconds
incapacitation duration: 12–40 seconds (seizure), 3–8 minutes (post-ictal disorientation)
charges per capacitor: 14 full discharges
recharge time: 8 seconds between activations
weight: 1.8 kg (gauntlet and forearm capacitor unit)
shielding defeat: Effective against targets with less than 4mm ferrous cranial shielding
power source: Forearm-mounted burst capacitor, induction rechargeable
tactical_use: The SOG-3 is a close-quarters control weapon, deployed by operators who need targets alive, compliant, or simply non-functional for a defined window. In extraction operations, a single application drops a target without the mess of conventional violence. In interrogation-adjacent contexts, the post-ictal disorientation period — during which targets are conscious but cognitively impaired and highly suggestible — is considered operationally useful by those willing to work in ethically ambiguous territory. Operators typically pair the gauntlet with a conventional weapon in the off hand, as the SOG-3 requires deliberate contact to activate.
cultural_context: The SOG-3 carries a particular stigma in GLMZ's augmentation communities because of its documented tendency to corrupt neural implants. Losing a memory implant to a Seizure hit is not just a medical emergency — it can mean the permanent loss of years of stored experience, professional credentials embedded in hardware, or personality-adjacent cognitive modifications. In some subcultures, surviving a SOG-3 hit with a fried implant is spoken of almost like a death — 'the person they were' is gone. This has made the gauntlet a weapon associated with targeted erasure rather than simple violence, and those who carry it are viewed with a particular kind of hostility.
known_users: Sienna Vrak (bounty hunter, known for delivering targets in post-ictal states)
The Undercurrent (data-theft collective rumored to use SOG-3s to wipe rival operators' memory implants)
story_hooks: A player character is hit with a SOG-3 during an ambush and wakes up missing the last six months of memories stored on their neural implant — including something someone clearly didn't want them to remember.
A Zheng-Dao Bioelectric executive is found in a catatonic state with a burned-out cognitive implant. The SOG-3 used was an inside job — it's registered to their own security division.
A street-level operator is selling SOG-3 knockoffs built from scavenged components. The quality control is catastrophic — some units don't stop at 0.08 seconds.
The players are hired to deliver a corporate whistleblower alive and cognitively intact, but the extraction route is guarded by a team known to carry Seizure gauntlets.
